items.title: Define one canonical background-aware liveness policy for dispatched agents
items.context: Centralize the user-visible semantics: elapsed time alone never proves a stall; query host-native status after the initial check; continue bounded monitoring while running/background; unknown remains monitor-only; only conclusive terminal evidence authorizes restart.

happy.desc: Given a dispatched agent whose authoritative host state remains foreground or running for more than 600 seconds and then completes, the canonical policy requires periodic host-status monitoring, never treats elapsed time or silence alone as a stall, starts no replacement, and accepts the original terminal result.

Given a dispatched agent that moves into a host-reported background state and completes after ten minutes, the policy keeps the same task identity under bounded repeated monitoring and delivers that late result without launching a duplicate worker or reviewer.

edge.desc: When the host status lookup is unavailable, transiently inconsistent, or returns unknown, the policy records the uncertainty and remains monitor-only; it neither infers death nor dispatches or restarts another agent until a later authoritative observation resolves the state.

A sequence of nonterminal observations such as silent, foreground, background, running, and unknown may cross both the four-minute check and 600-second mark without authorizing replacement; repeated checks remain bounded and target the original task identity.

adversarial.desc: Restart is authorized only by an authoritative terminal failure, cancellation, confirmed missing task or process, or equivalent conclusive dead-state signal; stale status, absence of output, elapsed time, and ambiguous lookup errors are explicitly insufficient, and an authorized retry is initiated at most once for that terminal attempt.

The host-managed dispatch liveness policy does not remove, widen, or reinterpret explicit configured subprocess timeout behavior: bounded provider.codex and cross_host_review executions still terminate and fail closed according to their timeout and policy ceilings.

items.userSees: Agent task <id> is still running or in the background; continue monitoring the same task. If status is unknown, do not start a duplicate. Restart once only when the host reports failed, cancelled, or missing/dead.
excludes: Changing provider.codex or cross_host_review explicit subprocess deadlines
Adding a new scheduler or host task-status API

verificationEvidence.note: State matrix keeps >600s foreground/running on the original identity with zero replacement.
State matrix keeps >600s background work on the original identity and accepts its late result once.
Unknown and unavailable observations remain monitor-only without duplicate dispatch.
All nonterminal observations ignore elapsedMs for replacement decisions.
Only authoritative terminal states authorize one replacement; repeat terminal observations are held.
Cross-host bounded timeout and fail-closed policy ceiling remain enforced.

items.title: Apply the liveness policy to every INIT, PLAN, DEV, and REVIEW dispatch hint
items.context: Replace the duplicated 4-minute/10-minute restart wording in story_create, story_dispatch, transition effects, and INIT guard recovery guidance so no production entrypoint retains elapsed-time-only restart advice.

happy.desc: An exhaustive registry-driven check renders every active canonical dispatch role, compatibility alias, allowed target kind, and allowed INIT, PLAN, DEV, or REVIEW phase, and each prompt carries one semantically identical canonical policy covering startup identity, host-native status queries, running and background monitoring, unknown-state non-duplication, and terminal-evidence-only restart.

Runtime guidance outside the common dispatch builder, including story_create INIT reviewer instructions, both INIT reviewer prompt variants, PLAN special reviewer prompts, missing-init-check guard recovery, DEV item or repair prompts, and REVIEW transition next steps, directs the host to inspect and monitor the existing task rather than restart it at an elapsed-time threshold.

verification.selector: init check required agents smoke passed

edge.desc: Special-case prompt builders that bypass the ordinary item or story reviewer path, including product-reviewer and topology or scope paths, cannot omit or contradict the canonical liveness semantics; aliases produce the same policy without stale copied wording.

Existing mandatory result-recording and role-boundary instructions remain intact while liveness text changes: INIT reviewers still call init_check_set, verification-intent never completes an item, implementers and repair workers retain their commit and resolution duties, and REVIEW lanes still use signed review-run evidence.

verification.selector: review pass and discard smoke passed

adversarial.desc: A production-source and generated-runtime scan fails if any active INIT, PLAN, DEV, or REVIEW hint still says that four or ten minutes of silence means stuck or stalled, advises restart from elapsed time alone, or makes the latest duplicate result authoritative.

The canonical wording cannot be diluted to vague keep waiting prose: every effective hint must explicitly separate running or background, unknown, and conclusive terminal states, and must prohibit duplicate dispatch while state is nonterminal or unknown.

items.userSees: After ten minutes without a result, every INIT, PLAN, DEV, and REVIEW hint says to inspect the existing task and keep monitoring it unless the host reports a terminal failure.
excludes: Changing provider.codex or cross_host_review explicit subprocess deadlines
Adding a new scheduler or host task-status API

items.title: Add regression coverage for long-running foreground and background agent semantics
items.context: Update source smokes so they fail on ten-minute restart language and require explicit running/background monitoring, unknown-state non-duplication, and terminal-evidence-only restart across item dispatch, INIT guidance, and REVIEW next steps.

happy.desc: A regression state-matrix simulates foreground and background agents that remain alive beyond 600 seconds and later succeed; at every intermediate observation the selected action is monitor the same task with zero restarts, and the eventual completion is consumed exactly once.

Focused CLI smokes exercise the effective story_create, dispatch, INIT guard recovery, DEV dispatch, and REVIEW next-step outputs and prove that all production entrypoints expose the canonical policy after source build synchronization.

verification.selector: review pass and discard smoke passed

edge.desc: A repeated unknown or temporarily unreachable host-status sequence, including observations before and after ten minutes, produces monitor-only decisions with preserved task identity and zero duplicate launches; a later running or completed observation resumes the same task.

Distinct conclusive terminal inputs such as failed, cancelled, and authoritatively missing task or process authorize a single restart, while a retry records the prior terminal reason and cannot be mistaken for a review or implementation conclusion from the dead attempt.

adversarial.desc: Mutation coverage replaces running, background, or unknown with restart and must fail, and replacing terminal failure with monitor-only must also fail, proving both the no-premature-restart boundary and the recover-from-confirmed-death boundary.

Regression coverage fails on residual ten-minute or four-minute elapsed-only restart wording across active source and generated outputs, while allowing explicit bounded subprocess timeout text only in the separate provider and cross-host execution contract.

Existing provider.codex and cross_host_review timeout tests continue to prove configured timeout enforcement, policy-ceiling tightening, fail-closed terminal classification, and the documented bounded retry behavior; the dispatch-liveness change must not make those subprocess tests weaker or remove them.
